description: A memory-only eight-centroid layer17 span program, frozen before future queries, reduces one 34-row Qwen correction-span representation from 69632 to 16480 serialized bytes and improves native first-logit fidelity over deletion on two later questions. Exact numerator omission factors into lost within-cluster exponential-score dispersion and finite exponential-score/value dependence, plus a small stored-primary arithmetic remainder. Both principal terms are substantial and their alignment changes with the query; correcting the denominator alone does not generally recover the numerator. Build and evaluate a source-only response representation that retains both effects, then repeated own-query use and memory updates after original selected-span K/V is made unavailable. Current result substitutes one read, retains the full model/cache and later native memory reads, and establishes neither ongoing compact sufficient chat nor serving savings.

A standard signed-byte row representation preserves all 34 paired exponential atoms at 17,984 serialized bytes versus 16,480 for centroids and 69,632 native bytes. Across 89 successive layer17 reads in three linked own-token turns, with original C17 K/V poisoned and dense fallback refused, mean numerator error is 2.086% versus centroids' 48.438%; all six sparse logit differences are below 0.1%. Exact34 parity, custody and Astra's independent FP64 audit agree. All answers also agree with deletion; every Q17 stays native because earlier layers and token histories match. This is recurring replacement of a fixed span, without physical allocation savings, changed-query feedback, new-memory compression or constant-size chat. Next: encode each actual own-state positioned new K/V row, atomically append codes/scales/position, consume the encoded row in the current and later reads, invalidate original row access, and roll back the encoded cursor with token state. Count 528 bytes per layer/token plus metadata/workspace versus 2,048 FP32 bytes; distinguish same-row quantization error from native-trajectory drift. Then test stacked layers and actual physical ownership.
